key_insight: Exactly enforcing boundary and initial conditions in a physics-informed neural network enables accurate recovery of the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support nondestructive characterization of shear electromechanical coupling in PMUTs and SAW devices without dedicated destructive resonance tests.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers in network outputs to enforce clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial conditions.
Train on coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and sparse observations, eliminating boundary and initial-condition penalty weights.
Nondimensionalize governing coefficients to comparable scales; use a quadratic temporal multiplier to improve early-time electrostatic consistency.
evidence_signal: In six-way manufactured-data comparisons at 30 dB, constrained variants achieved 0.15–0.51% mean e15 error; the full formulation achieved 1.19% on finite-element data at 30 dB and 0.65–2.71% across 40–0 dB.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; experimental robustness to model mismatch and imperfectly known boundary conditions remains unverified.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
